newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediobanca details eurolira convertible bond.
newsitem.headline: Mediobanca details eurolira convertible bond.

text.p: Italian merchant bank Mediobanca said it was coordinating the issue of five-year Mediobanca International eurolira bonds convertible into shares in Italian insurer Alleanza.
A Mediobanca statement said the merchant bank was global coordinator to the Mediobanca International 1997-2002 two-percent bond issue which is for a nominal value of 830 billion lire.
The bonds are exchangeable into 53 million ordinary Alleanza shares held by Assicurazioni Generali, representing 8.7 percent of Alleanza's ordinary share capital.
Joint lead managers are Goldman Sachs International and Paribas and the offer is open to Italian professional and foreign institutional investors, excluding the United States, Canada and Japan.
Provision had been made to issue additional exchangeable bonds in an amount of about 15 percent of the offering to cover any overallotment.
It said assuming all the bonds were exchanged, Generali would retain its absolute majority in Alleanza's share capital.

Bookbuilding runs from May 20-21 and indicative parameters were yield to maturity from 4-7/8 to 5-3/8 and an issue price between 85.3-87.3 percent of the nominal lira price with a premium in lira of 12-15 percent over Alleanza's share price.
Pricing will be around May 21 and Mediobanca confirmed an application had been made to list on the Luxembourg stock exchange.
